hypotheses.claim: A CSM can set X-Acting-As-Zone for a zone whose ZM has NO role_unavailability window and the backend accepts it, stamping acted_as_role — no cascade check runs.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: A guard or interceptor upstream of the decorator validates the header against role_unavailability before resolveActingContext runs.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'currentActingRoleForZone|isRoleUnavailable' apps/backend/src --exclude-dir=generated | grep -v src/roles/ -> zero hits; only resolveActingContext consumes the header (current-actor/current-scope decorators, manager-scope.ts)

hypotheses.claim: A write through leave-request / intraday-updates / tickets while acting stores actedAsRole NULL, so the acting action is indistinguishable from an own-scope one in audit_logs.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The service layer re-derives actedAsRole from the request instead of trusting the controller's literal null.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'auditActor(' apps/backend/src -> 24 files, none of them these controllers' services; audit.service.ts:66 writes entry.actedAsRole ?? null with no re-derivation

hypotheses.claim: csm-approval-share returns zeros or near-zeros in practice because the acting writes that would populate acting_zone are the same ones passing actedAsRole:null.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Enough audit sites do use auditActor() that the report still has a representative sample.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'actedAsRole: null' apps/backend/src --exclude-dir=generated -> 11 controller sites, all on manager write paths a CSM would use while acting

hypotheses.claim: Repeated POST /api/auth/login with wrong passwords is never blocked or slowed — no throttler, no lockout, no counter.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: Rate limiting sits at a reverse proxy / platform layer outside apps/backend.
hypotheses.altCheck: grep -rn 'Throttler|throttle|rate-limit|rateLimit' apps/backend/src apps/backend/package.json -> 0 hits; no nginx/ingress config in repo referencing limit_req

hypotheses.claim: Clearing sessionStorage is the only 'exit' — a stale acting header from another tab or a restored session re-enters acting scope with no server-side revocation.
hypotheses.strongestAlternative: The access token itself carries the acting zone, so exit invalidates it server-side.
hypotheses.altCheck: apps/backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:54 signAccessToken claims are {user_id, role, zone_id} only — no acting zone in the token; acting is header-only
